nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a pushdown automaton and let $\Gamma_0$ be a finite set of stack symbols of $M$ that contains the initial stack symbol of $M$ and is closed for $M$. Then the restriction of $M$ to the stack alphabet $\Gamma_0$ accepts, by empty stack, exactly the same language as $M$.
nodes.title: Restricting the stack alphabet preserves the accepted language

nodes.summary: The language accepted by a pushdown automaton $M$, by empty stack, consists of the words $w$ for which some computation of $M$ leads from the initial configuration on input $w$ to a configuration, in some state, with no remaining input and an empty stack.
nodes.title: Language accepted by a pushdown automaton

nodes.title: Computations extend by unread input and stack bottom

nodes.summary: A finite set $\Gamma_0$ of stack symbols is closed for a pushdown automaton $M$ when every transition of $M$ that pops a symbol in $\Gamma_0$, from any state and on any input letter or on $\varepsilon$, pushes only symbols in $\Gamma_0$. Computations starting with a stack inside a closed set keep their stack inside it.
nodes.title: Closed sets of stack symbols

nodes.summary: A configuration of a pushdown automaton with input alphabet $T$, states in $\sigma$ and stack alphabet $\Gamma$ consists of a current state in $\sigma$, the remaining unread input (a word over $T$), and the stack contents (a list over $\Gamma$ whose first element is the top of the stack).

nodes.title: Computations of the restriction are computations of the automaton

nodes.summary: For a pushdown automaton $M$, a configuration $c$ derives a configuration $c'$ when $M$ can reach $c'$ from $c$ in zero or more computation steps; that is, derivation is the reflexive transitive closure of the one-step computation relation of $M$.

nodes.title: Finitely supported pushdown automata

nodes.summary: The initial configuration of a pushdown automaton $M$ on an input word $w$ has the start state of $M$ as its state, all of $w$ as its remaining input, and the stack consisting of the initial stack symbol of $M$ alone.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
